claims.text: The conventionally cast eutectic AlCoCrFeNi-based alloy has a coarse eutectic microstructure with distinct interphase boundaries.
Adding approximately 0.5 at% Nb and applying solution annealing followed by tempering will produce homogeneously distributed nanoscale Nb-rich precipitates.
The Nb-rich precipitates will be located primarily along eutectic interphase boundaries.
Controlled heat treatment can induce strengthening nanoscale precipitates in eutectic AlCoCrFeNi-based alloys.
Nb-rich precipitates will impede dislocation motion and increase strength through precipitation strengthening.
The Nb-rich precipitates will blunt crack tips.
The Nb-rich precipitates will promote uniform plastic deformation and delay strain localization.
Crack-tip blunting and delayed strain localization will improve tensile ductility.
Optimizing precipitate size and distribution will prevent the precipitates from causing embrittlement.
The Nb-modified and heat-treated alloy will have approximately 15–20% higher yield strength than the baseline alloy.
The Nb-modified and heat-treated alloy will have approximately 10–15% greater tensile elongation than the baseline alloy.
Precipitation heat treatment can substantially increase yield strength in an AlCoCrFeNi-based eutectic alloy.
Precipitation heat treatment can simultaneously increase strength and ductility in the proposed Nb-modified alloy.
The proposed benefit should hold under controlled cooling, optimized heat treatment, and room-temperature quasi-static tensile loading.
Departures from the optimal Nb content or heat treatment may create an inhomogeneous precipitate distribution and limit simultaneous strength and ductility enhancement.
The baseline contains no Nb and receives no specialized thermal treatment for precipitate control.

contradictions.description: The baseline is defined as receiving no specialized thermal treatment, but the experiment says the Nb-free control and Nb-added samples will have identical processing aside from Nb addition. These descriptions imply different control treatments and therefore test different causal contrasts.

The hypothesized intervention combines Nb addition with an optimized thermal treatment, whereas the experimental design states that Nb addition is the only processing difference between groups. It is therefore unclear whether the experiment tests the combined intervention or isolates only the Nb effect.
